The spectrum potentially allocated to mobile service on a primary basis includes 7.145 8.5, 10 13.25, 14.3 15.35, 17.7 19.7, and 21.2 23.6 GHz, accumulating in an aggregate bandwidth of approximately 9 GHz. For such systems, a multiband and highly integrated multiplexer would be a key component to enable multiple RF (Radio Frequency) chains to share a common antenna aperture for terminals communicating with both TN/NTN. This feature is particularly attractive in the implementation of hybrid User Terminals for 6G, where up to five bands need to be separated.This activity will develop a wideband multiplexer breadboard using advanced RF filtering and packaging techniques, enabling hybrid terrestrial/satcom 6G NTN services within the same antenna aperture.
